argument.notes: S001 sums at most h/tau+1 residual increments, including partial endpoints, and bounds e' by C_M E_I+C_M(tau^gamma+E_I) in H^(-pstar), giving the asserted X estimates. S002's differentiated terms combine as C(e,g,g)-C(e,g,e)/2=C(e,g,V), with g=v-e/2; the forcing signs and coefficients are correct and both boundary values contribute C_M N^(-1)E_I. In S003 the high-input decomposition yields h times the product of X norms plus N^(-pstar) times the product of L2 norms. Each cubic term contains e, giving C_M h tau^gamma+C_M(h+N^(-pstar))E_I. On a step portion of length ell<=tau, the forcing terms C(Y,z,V) and C(Y,Y,V) are bounded respectively by C_M(ell q_n+tau q_n) and C_M(ell q_n^2+tau q_n^2), hence by C_M tau q_n. The W term is bounded by (ell/tau)C_M||W||_2||V||_2<=C_M ell q_n. Summation gives the stated forcing bound. S004 combines these with the low-frequency bound and residual estimate to obtain precisely N010. No limiting exchange is needed; continuity and finite piecewise integration suffice.

background_notes.fact: For a continuous function with values in a Sobolev Hilbert space that is C1 on each of finitely many time pieces, its distributional derivative is its piecewise derivative, and f(t)-f(a)=integral_a^t f'(s) ds. For an integrable Hilbert-space-valued G, ||integral_J G||<=integral_J||G||. Restriction to a subinterval does not increase either component of X. Sobolev norms dominate L2 when the exponent is nonnegative.

background_notes.justification: Apply the fundamental theorem of calculus on each smooth time piece and add the resulting increments; the interior endpoint values cancel by continuity. Integration by parts against a scalar test function gives the same cancellation and no jump distributions. The integral norm inequality follows by testing against unit vectors and the scalar integral inequality. Essential suprema decrease upon restriction. Finally <k>^(2s)>=1 for s>=0 gives the Sobolev comparison directly.

background_notes.justification: A 0/1 multiplier decreases each weighted coefficient square sum and commutes with the time derivative, giving X contraction even when N/3<1. On |k|>N/3, <k>^(-pstar)<=(N/3)^(-pstar), proving the tail estimate. Multiplication adds frequencies; three factors supported in |k|<=N/3 have product support in |k|<=N. All intervening multipliers, projections and time integration preserve this support. For nonzero integer k, |k|^(-1)<=1. Finally on 0<|k|<=N the multiplier ratio between partial_x and Dinv is of absolute value k^2<=N^2. These coefficient inequalities prove the remaining norm bounds.
